children: Strategy founder Michael Saylor said in a Bloomberg interview that the potential removal of MSTR under MSCI’s new index rules would have limited importance to Strategy because the funds controlled by MSCI are relatively small. According to ChainCatcher, Saylor said he was disappointed with MSCI’s position, arguing that counting oil, gas, land and machinery as capital while excluding Bitcoin reflects a value judgment and bias against digital assets.

Saylor compared MSCI’s stance to that of unregistered financial advisers and said it sets a bad precedent for the industry. He called digital assets the future and said investors and the United States would not agree with MSCI rejecting that future. He added that withdrawing the proposal to remove MSTR would benefit the broader industry.

On the debate over whether Strategy has an operating business, Saylor compared it with banks and insurance companies, which sell credit and policies. He said Strategy uses Bitcoin to support digital credit products, making it an operating company that should be treated like other financial firms.

title: Michael Saylor Says Potential MSCI Removal of MSTR Is Not Crucial to Strategy, Urges Reconsideration
